slogans.title: First, train in the preliminaries
slogans.explanation: The four reminders, or four mind-changings, are contemplations that help you to appreciate the rarity and preciousness of human life. These preparations are necessary to open your mind and heart to the Dharma and to begin the journey of mind training. Begin by reflecting on the precious human birth you have been given, then recognize that death and impermanence surround all of us. Consider the suffering that arises from unskillful actions, and finally contemplate the nature of suffering in samsara. These four reflections are the ground from which genuine practice grows.

slogans.title: Regard all dharmas as dreams
slogans.explanation: This slogan is about developing the understanding that all experiences and perceptions are dreamlike and not ultimately real. Just as a dream feels very real while you are dreaming but is revealed as an illusion when you wake up, all of our experiences in waking life can be understood in the same way. This practice helps to loosen our attachment to things and experiences, as we come to see them as temporary and insubstantial. When we understand that reality is like a dream, we can let go of our clinging and open ourselves to a deeper understanding of the nature of existence.

slogans.title: Examine the nature of unborn awareness
slogans.explanation: This slogan asks us to look into the nature of our own awareness and to see that it does not have a beginning, middle, or end. It is unborn, meaning that it has never been created and will never be destroyed. When we look at our own awareness, we do not find anything solid or substantial. Instead, we find an openness and clarity that is beyond any concepts or labels we might put on it. This is the nature of mind, which is sometimes called Buddha-nature or rigpa. By examining this nature, we can begin to understand the true nature of ourselves and the world.

slogans.title: Self-liberate even the antidote
slogans.explanation: This slogan is asking us to let go of even the spiritual practices and methods we use to help us on the path to enlightenment. The idea is that even our spiritual practices can become attachments or obstacles if we cling to them too tightly. We need to be willing to let them go when they have served their purpose. This means not getting too caught up in any particular practice or technique, and being open to moving on when the time is right. It also means trusting in the process and letting go of the need to control or manipulate our spiritual journey.

slogans.title: Rest in the nature of alaya, the essence
slogans.explanation: Alaya is a Sanskrit term that refers to the ground of all experience, the underlying essence or nature of mind. Resting in the nature of alaya means becoming familiar with this ground, which is the nature of all phenomena. This is a practice of meditation, where we learn to recognize and rest in the open, spacious awareness that underlies all of our experience. By resting in this nature, we begin to understand that our thoughts, feelings, and perceptions are not as solid or real as they seem. We can see through the illusions of the ego and experience a deeper sense of peace and clarity.

slogans.title: In the post-meditation period, be a child of illusion
slogans.explanation: This slogan refers to the practice of maintaining a sense of open, childlike awareness even after formal meditation sessions. Just as a child experiences the world with fresh, wide-open eyes, we can cultivate a similar sense of wonder and openness in our daily lives. This means seeing all experiences as illusory and not getting too caught up in our thoughts and emotions. We can learn to witness our experiences without being controlled by them, maintaining a sense of spaciousness and clarity even in the midst of the busyness of daily life.

slogans.title: Sending and taking should be practiced alternately. These two should ride the breath
slogans.explanation: This slogan refers to the tonglen practice, which is a method for training the mind in compassion and the exchange of self and other. In tonglen, we breathe in the suffering of others and breathe out love and compassion to them. This practice helps to develop empathy and compassion for others, and to see beyond our own self-centered concerns. By alternating between sending and taking, we learn to open our hearts and minds to the suffering of others, and to cultivate a genuine wish to help them. Riding the breath refers to synchronizing the practice with the natural rhythm of the breath, which helps to ground and deepen the practice.

slogans.title: Three objects, three poisons, three seeds of virtue
slogans.explanation: The three objects are friends, enemies, and neutrals. The three poisons are attachment, aversion, and ignorance. The three seeds of virtue are the antidotes to these poisons: non-attachment, compassion, and wisdom. This slogan reminds us to be mindful of our reactions to the people and situations we encounter and to use them as opportunities to cultivate virtue. When we feel attachment to a friend, we can practice non-attachment. When we feel aversion to an enemy, we can practice compassion. When we feel indifference to a neutral person, we can practice wisdom. By using these reactions as seeds of virtue, we can transform our everyday experiences into opportunities for spiritual growth.

slogans.title: In all activities, train with slogans
slogans.explanation: This slogan encourages us to use the Lojong slogans as a guide for all of our activities, both on and off the meditation cushion. The slogans can serve as reminders to maintain mindfulness and compassion in all of our actions. By memorizing and reflecting on the slogans, we can bring their wisdom into our daily lives and use them as a guide for how to act and think. This is a way of integrating our spiritual practice into all aspects of our lives, rather than just limiting it to formal meditation sessions.

slogans.title: Begin the sequence of sending and taking with yourself
slogans.explanation: This slogan encourages us to begin the practice of tonglen by directing loving-kindness and compassion toward ourselves. This means starting the practice of sending and taking by acknowledging and taking care of our own suffering and needs before we try to help others. It's important to develop self-compassion and to nurture ourselves before we can truly help others. By beginning with ourselves, we can develop a solid foundation of self-love and self-acceptance, which will then allow us to extend that love and compassion to others.

slogans.title: When the world is filled with evil, transform all mishaps into the path of bodhi
slogans.explanation: This slogan encourages us to use adversity as a teacher and to transform all difficult situations into opportunities for spiritual growth. The word 'bodhi' means 'awakening' or 'enlightenment' in Sanskrit. When we face difficult or challenging situations, we can choose to see them as opportunities to develop our inner strength, resilience, and wisdom. This slogan is asking us to change our perspective on adversity and to see it as a part of the path to enlightenment, rather than as a hindrance. By transforming our mishaps into the path of bodhi, we can grow and evolve spiritually, even in the midst of difficult circumstances.

slogans.title: Drive all blames into one
slogans.explanation: This slogan asks us to stop blaming others for our problems and instead look at ourselves to find the root cause. Instead of pointing the finger at others, we are asked to accept that we are responsible for our own experience. By 'driving all blames into one', we focus our attention inward and examine our own mind, thoughts, and actions. We realize that much of our suffering is the result of our own ego-driven thoughts and actions. This doesn't mean that we are to blame for everything that happens to us; rather, it's about taking responsibility for our own reactions and responses to what happens.

slogans.title: Be grateful to everyone
slogans.explanation: This slogan teaches us to be grateful for all of our experiences, even those that are difficult or unpleasant. Every person and situation we encounter is an opportunity to learn and grow, and we can be grateful for that. Even our enemies or adversaries can serve as teachers, showing us where we have work to do in ourselves. By cultivating a sense of gratitude for all of our experiences, we can shift our perspective and see the good in even the most difficult situations. Gratitude opens our hearts and allows us to see the gifts that life brings us, even when they don't appear that way on the surface.

slogans.title: Seeing confusion as the four kayas is unsurpassable shunyata protection
slogans.explanation: This slogan refers to the practice of seeing the confusion or chaos of our ordinary experience as an expression of the four kayas, or forms of enlightened being. The four kayas are the dharmakaya, sambhogakaya, nirmanakaya, and svabhavikakaya. By seeing the confusion and chaos of our daily lives as an expression of these enlightened forms, we can find a sense of peace and stability even in the midst of turmoil. This is a way of transforming our experience of confusion into a protection or shield against suffering. The term 'shunyata' refers to the Buddhist concept of emptiness, or the absence of a fixed, permanent self.

slogans.title: Four practices are the best of methods
slogans.explanation: The four practices referred to in this slogan are accumulating merit, laying down negativities, offering to the dons (spirits or forces), and making offerings to the dharmapalas (protectors of the dharma). These four practices are said to be the most effective methods for working with adversity and for making progress on the spiritual path. By engaging in these practices regularly, we can purify our negative karma, accumulate positive karma, and create the conditions for greater enlightenment and freedom.

slogans.title: Whatever you meet unexpectedly, join with meditation
slogans.explanation: This slogan teaches us to be mindful and present in all of our experiences, no matter how unexpected or difficult. When we encounter something unexpected, we have a choice about how to respond. We can react with fear, anger, or confusion, or we can choose to join the experience with our meditation practice. This means remaining present, open, and curious, even in the face of unexpected challenges. By joining our experiences with meditation, we can transform them from obstacles into opportunities for growth and insight.

slogans.title: Practice the five strengths, the condensed heart instructions
slogans.explanation: The five strengths are: determination, familiarization, the positive seed, reproach, and aspiration. Determination means committing to the practice with a clear intention. Familiarization means practicing regularly and consistently. The positive seed means cultivating positive qualities and virtuous actions. Reproach means recognizing and correcting our negative habits and tendencies. Aspiration means maintaining a clear vision of what we are trying to achieve through our practice. These five strengths are considered to be the most essential elements of the Lojong practice, and are said to encompass the entire teachings in a condensed form.

slogans.title: The Mahayana instruction for ejection of consciousness at death is the five strengths: how you conduct yourself is important
slogans.explanation: This slogan refers to the practice of phowa, or the ejection of consciousness at the time of death. The five strengths mentioned here are the same as those in the previous slogan, and they are to be applied to the practice of dying. At the time of death, it is said that the mind has a great opportunity for liberation, and the practice of the five strengths can help to ensure that we make the most of this opportunity. By cultivating these qualities throughout our lives, we can prepare ourselves for a conscious and liberated death.

slogans.title: All dharma agrees at one point
slogans.explanation: This slogan reminds us that all of the different schools and traditions of Buddhism share a common purpose: to reduce our ego-clinging and to cultivate compassion and wisdom. Despite the many different methods and approaches, all Buddhist teachings are ultimately pointing in the same direction: toward the liberation from suffering and the realization of our true nature. This slogan encourages us to focus on this common purpose and to not get too caught up in the differences and distinctions between different schools or traditions.

slogans.title: Of the two witnesses, hold the principal one
slogans.explanation: The two witnesses referred to in this slogan are ourselves and others. The slogan is asking us to hold ourselves as the principal witness and to be honest and self-aware about our own thoughts, feelings, and actions. This is about taking responsibility for our own experience and not projecting our problems onto others. Instead of looking outside of ourselves for validation or confirmation, we are asked to look within and to trust our own inner wisdom. By holding ourselves as the principal witness, we can develop greater self-awareness and take greater responsibility for our own spiritual growth.

slogans.title: Always maintain only a joyful mind
slogans.explanation: This slogan asks us to cultivate a positive and joyful mental attitude in all circumstances. This doesn't mean that we should ignore or suppress negative emotions, but rather that we should cultivate an underlying sense of joy and appreciation for life. We can do this by focusing on the positive aspects of our experience, cultivating gratitude for what we have, and by practicing loving-kindness and compassion toward ourselves and others. By maintaining a joyful mind, we can create a more positive and uplifting inner environment, which will in turn influence our external circumstances.

slogans.title: If you can practice even when distracted, you are well trained
slogans.explanation: This slogan tells us that a sign of progress in practice is the ability to maintain mindfulness even in the midst of distractions. When we are beginners in meditation or other spiritual practices, it can be difficult to maintain our focus and presence when we are surrounded by distractions. But as we develop greater skill and experience, we become more able to stay present and mindful even in challenging or distracting environments. This slogan is encouraging us to persevere in our practice, knowing that the ability to remain mindful even when distracted is a sign that we are making progress.

slogans.title: Always abide by the three basic principles
slogans.explanation: The three basic principles referred to in this slogan are: keeping your commitments, not acting ostentatiously, and developing patience. Keeping your commitments means following through on your spiritual vows and intentions. Not acting ostentatiously means not showing off or seeking attention for your spiritual practice. Developing patience means cultivating the ability to remain calm and composed in the face of difficulties or challenges. These three principles are considered to be foundational to the practice of Lojong and to the cultivation of a healthy and balanced spiritual life.

slogans.title: Change your attitude, but remain natural
slogans.explanation: This slogan is asking us to cultivate a positive and compassionate attitude toward ourselves and others, while still remaining natural and authentic. It's about changing our inner attitude and perspective, rather than trying to change our external behavior or appearance. We are encouraged to develop a more open, compassionate, and accepting way of relating to ourselves and others, but without becoming artificial or forced in our behavior. The idea is to allow our inner transformation to naturally and organically express itself in our outer life, without trying to force or fake it.

slogans.title: Don't talk about injured limbs
slogans.explanation: This slogan advises us not to talk about or dwell on the flaws or weaknesses of others. Instead of criticizing or gossiping about others, we should focus on their positive qualities and try to see the best in them. This is a practice of cultivating compassion and kindness toward others, and of refraining from harmful speech. By not talking about the injured limbs of others, we can create a more positive and supportive environment, and we can avoid contributing to the suffering of others through harmful words.

slogans.title: Don't ponder others
slogans.explanation: This slogan is telling us not to spend time thinking about or analyzing the faults or failings of others. Instead of focusing on the flaws of others, we should turn our attention inward and work on our own spiritual development. This is a practice of cultivating non-judgmental awareness and compassion toward others, and of refraining from harsh or critical thinking. By not pondering others in a negative way, we can cultivate a more open and accepting attitude toward those around us.

slogans.title: Work with the greatest defilements first
slogans.explanation: This slogan tells us to focus our spiritual efforts on the most prominent and powerful negative qualities in ourselves. Rather than trying to work on all of our negative qualities at once, we should identify and work with the ones that are causing us the most difficulty and suffering. This is a way of making the most efficient use of our spiritual efforts and of making the most significant progress. By working with our greatest defilements first, we can make the most meaningful changes in ourselves and can create the most positive impact on our own lives and the lives of others.

slogans.title: Abandon any hope of fruition
slogans.explanation: This slogan is advising us to practice for its own sake, rather than for any hoped-for results or outcomes. We should let go of our attachment to the fruits of our practice and instead focus on the process itself. This is a practice of non-attachment, which is a key principle in Buddhist teaching. By abandoning our hope for fruition, we can approach our practice with a more open and accepting attitude, and we can avoid getting caught up in disappointment or frustration when things don't go as we hoped.

slogans.title: Abandon poisonous food
slogans.explanation: This slogan refers to actions, thoughts, or experiences that are harmful to our spiritual health and wellbeing. Just as we would avoid eating food that is poisonous to our physical health, we should also avoid things that are harmful to our spiritual wellbeing. This includes things like gossip, harmful speech, or engaging in activities that feed our negative emotions and habits. By abandoning these poisonous elements from our lives, we can create a more positive and nourishing environment for our spiritual practice to flourish.

slogans.title: Don't be so predictable
slogans.explanation: This slogan is urging us to be adaptable and flexible in our spiritual practice, rather than getting stuck in rigid patterns of behavior. We should be willing to change and evolve as our practice deepens and as our understanding of the teachings grows. This also means being open to new approaches and methods, and not getting too attached to any particular way of doing things. By not being so predictable, we can keep our practice fresh and alive, and avoid getting stuck in unhelpful ruts or habits.

slogans.title: Don't malign others
slogans.explanation: This slogan advises us not to speak ill of others or to engage in gossip and criticism. When we malign others, we create negative karma for ourselves and contribute to suffering in the world. Instead, we should try to see the best in others and to speak about them in a positive and compassionate way. By refraining from maligning others, we can cultivate a more positive and supportive environment for ourselves and those around us.

slogans.title: Don't wait in ambush
slogans.explanation: This slogan warns against holding grudges or waiting for the opportunity to take revenge on those who have wronged us. Instead of waiting to get back at someone who has hurt us, we should try to let go of our resentment and to practice forgiveness and compassion. By not waiting in ambush, we can release ourselves from the burden of anger and resentment, and we can cultivate a more peaceful and harmonious inner life.

slogans.title: Don't bring things to a painful point
slogans.explanation: This slogan warns against saying or doing things that are hurtful or harmful to others. Sometimes, we might be tempted to make cutting remarks or to use our knowledge of others' vulnerabilities against them. This slogan reminds us to be mindful of the impact of our words and actions on others, and to avoid causing unnecessary pain or harm. By not bringing things to a painful point, we can cultivate a more compassionate and respectful way of relating to others.

slogans.title: Don't transfer the ox's load to the cow
slogans.explanation: This slogan warns against shifting our responsibilities and burdens onto others. Instead of passing the buck, we should take responsibility for our own actions and their consequences. This is a practice of cultivating self-reliance and integrity, and of respecting the boundaries and capacities of others. By not transferring the ox's load to the cow, we can develop greater self-reliance and a more honest and respectful way of relating to others.

slogans.title: Don't try to be the fastest
slogans.explanation: This slogan reminds us to not rush or try to outdo others in our spiritual practice. Instead, we should move at our own pace and focus on the quality of our practice, rather than trying to race ahead or to impress others. This is a practice of cultivating patience and humility, and of appreciating the journey, rather than focusing solely on the destination. By not trying to be the fastest, we can avoid the pitfall of spiritual materialism, in which we compete with others or try to use our practice to boost our ego.

slogans.title: Don't act with a twist
slogans.explanation: This slogan warns against doing things with hidden or ulterior motives. Instead of being genuine and sincere in our actions, we might be tempted to do things for our own selfish purposes, while pretending to be acting for the benefit of others. This is a form of deception that can harm our relationships and our spiritual practice. By not acting with a twist, we can cultivate a more honest and transparent way of relating to others and to our practice.

slogans.title: Don't make gods into demons
slogans.explanation: This slogan warns against twisting positive practices or relationships into something harmful. Sometimes, we might use our spiritual practice or our relationships with teachers and mentors in a way that feeds our ego or causes harm. This can happen when we become attached to the outer forms of practice, or when we project our own issues onto our teachers or the teachings. By not making gods into demons, we can keep our practice and our relationships with teachers healthy and balanced.

slogans.title: Don't seek others' pain as the limbs of your own happiness
slogans.explanation: This slogan warns against finding satisfaction or happiness at the expense of others' suffering. Sometimes, we might feel a perverse pleasure when others suffer, especially if we see them as having wronged us in some way. This kind of schadenfreude is harmful to our own spiritual development and to our relationships with others. By not seeking others' pain as the limbs of our own happiness, we can cultivate a more compassionate and empathetic way of relating to others.

slogans.title: All activities should be done with one intention
slogans.explanation: This slogan encourages us to approach all of our activities with a single, clear intention: to benefit all beings and to cultivate wisdom and compassion. By aligning all of our actions with this intention, we can transform even mundane activities into spiritual practice. This is a way of bringing mindfulness and intentionality into all aspects of our lives, rather than just limiting our practice to formal meditation sessions. When we approach all of our activities with this intention, we can make every moment an opportunity for spiritual growth and for contributing to the wellbeing of others.

slogans.title: Correct all wrongs with one intention
slogans.explanation: This slogan refers to the practice of using a single, clear intention to address and correct all of our negative actions and tendencies. The intention is to benefit all beings and to cultivate wisdom and compassion. By bringing this intention to all of our efforts to correct our wrongs, we can approach our mistakes with a spirit of openness and acceptance, rather than self-criticism and judgment. This is a way of transforming our approach to our own failings, and of seeing them as opportunities for growth rather than as sources of shame or guilt.

slogans.title: Two activities: one at the beginning, one at the end
slogans.explanation: This slogan refers to the practice of setting an intention at the beginning of the day and dedicating the merits of one's actions at the end of the day. By starting each day with a clear intention to benefit all beings, we can align our actions with this purpose throughout the day. At the end of the day, by dedicating the merits of our actions to all beings, we can reinforce our commitment to this intention and cultivate a sense of gratitude and generosity. These two activities serve as bookends to our daily practice, helping us to maintain mindfulness and intentionality throughout the day.

slogans.title: Whichever of the two occurs, be patient
slogans.explanation: This slogan refers to the practice of cultivating patience in both good times and bad. Whether we are experiencing pleasure or pain, success or failure, we should practice patience and equanimity. This means not getting too caught up in our reactions to external circumstances, and instead maintaining a steady, patient, and open attitude. By cultivating patience in all circumstances, we can develop a more stable and balanced inner life, and we can avoid getting swept up in the inevitable ups and downs of daily life.

slogans.title: Observe these two, even at the risk of your life
slogans.explanation: The two things referred to in this slogan are the general commitments of the Mahayana path (such as taking refuge in the three jewels) and the specific commitments of the Lojong practice (such as not seeking others' pain as the limbs of your own happiness). This slogan is urging us to honor and maintain these commitments, even in the most difficult or dangerous circumstances. By keeping these commitments, we can maintain our integrity and our connection to the teachings, and we can continue to make progress on the path even in the face of great adversity.

slogans.title: Train in the three difficulties
slogans.explanation: The three difficulties referred to in this slogan are: recognizing our neurosis, doing something about it, and breaking the habitual pattern. The first difficulty is recognizing when we are in the grip of a neurotic pattern of thinking or behavior. The second is finding the will and the means to address it. The third is breaking the habitual patterns that keep us stuck in the neurotic behavior. By training in these three difficulties, we can make progress in transforming our negative habits and tendencies, and we can cultivate a more positive and compassionate way of being in the world.

slogans.title: Take on the three principal causes
slogans.explanation: The three principal causes referred to in this slogan are: meeting a qualified teacher, practicing the dharma sincerely, and having the necessary material conditions to support the practice. These three causes are considered to be essential for making progress on the spiritual path. By cultivating these three causes, we can create the conditions necessary for deep and lasting spiritual growth. This means seeking out qualified teachers and teachings, committing to a sincere and regular practice, and taking care of our basic material needs so that we can focus our energy on our practice.

slogans.title: Pay heed that the three never wane
slogans.explanation: The three things that should never wane are: gratitude toward our teachers, appreciation for the opportunity to practice, and commitment to benefiting all beings. These three qualities are essential for maintaining a healthy and balanced spiritual practice. By keeping these three qualities alive and vibrant, we can continue to make progress on the path even in the face of challenges and difficulties. This slogan is asking us to regularly check in with ourselves and to make sure that these three qualities are still present and strong in our practice.

slogans.title: Keep the three inseparable
slogans.explanation: The three things that should be kept inseparable are: body, speech, and mind. This slogan is reminding us to maintain alignment and consistency between our thoughts, words, and actions. When our body, speech, and mind are all working together in harmony, we can live and practice with greater integrity and effectiveness. This means being mindful of our physical actions, our words, and our mental states, and striving to keep them all aligned with our deepest intentions and values.

slogans.title: Train without bias in all areas. It is crucial always to do this pervasively and wholeheartedly
slogans.explanation: This slogan is reminding us to practice Lojong in a comprehensive and impartial way, extending our compassion and care to all beings without discrimination. This means not favoring some beings over others, and not limiting our practice to only certain types of situations or relationships. By practicing without bias, we can cultivate a more genuine and universal compassion, one that extends to all beings without exception. This kind of impartial compassion is considered to be a key quality of the bodhisattva, who works for the benefit of all beings without distinction.

slogans.title: Always meditate on whatever provokes resentment
slogans.explanation: This slogan encourages us to use the things that provoke our anger, resentment, or aversion as objects of meditation. Instead of avoiding or suppressing these difficult emotions, we should turn toward them and examine them with openness and curiosity. By meditating on the things that provoke resentment, we can begin to understand the root causes of these emotions and to develop a more compassionate and equanimous relationship with them. This is a way of transforming our difficult emotions from obstacles into opportunities for growth and insight.

slogans.title: Don't be swayed by external circumstances
slogans.explanation: This slogan encourages us to maintain our inner stability and equanimity, even in the face of changing external circumstances. It's easy to feel destabilized or thrown off balance when things don't go according to plan, or when we face unexpected challenges or setbacks. But by maintaining a steady and grounded inner state, we can remain calm and centered even in the midst of turmoil. This slogan is asking us to cultivate a sense of inner resilience and stability, so that we are not at the mercy of the ups and downs of external circumstances.

slogans.title: This time, practice the main points
slogans.explanation: This slogan is a reminder to prioritize the most important elements of our spiritual practice. It's easy to get distracted by secondary or peripheral concerns, and to lose sight of the core practices that are most essential for our spiritual growth. This slogan is asking us to refocus on the main points of our practice, and to make sure that we are giving sufficient time and attention to the most important elements. By practicing the main points, we can ensure that our practice is well-founded and effective.

slogans.title: Don't misinterpret
slogans.explanation:
This slogan reminds us to take care not to misinterpret or misunderstand the world and our experiences. This means not jumping to conclusions, not getting caught up in unhelpful assumptions or judgments, and not allowing our preconceived notions to cloud our understanding. Instead, we should strive to see things clearly and objectively, and to be open and receptive to new information and perspectives. By not misinterpreting, we can avoid getting caught up in misunderstandings or conflicts, and we can cultivate a deeper understanding of ourselves and the world.

The six things that may be misinterpreted are patience, yearning, excitement, compassion, priorities and joy. You're patient when you're getting your way, but not when its difficult. You yearn for worldly things, instead of an open heart and mind. You get excited about wealth and entertainment, instead of your potential for enlightenment. You have compassion for those you like, but none for those you don't. Worldly gain is your priority rather than cultivating loving-kindness and compassion. You feel joy when your enemies suffer, and do not rejoice in others' good fortune.

slogans.title: Don't vacillate (in your practice of Lojong)
slogans.explanation: This slogan is meant to urge us to be resolute and decisive in our spiritual practice. This means not getting caught up in indecision or doubt, and not allowing ourselves to be swayed by external circumstances or distractions. Instead, we should strive to remain steady and focused, and to approach our practice with determination and commitment. By not vacillating, we can avoid getting sidetracked or discouraged, and we can make steady progress on the path towards enlightenment.

slogans.title: Train wholeheartedly
slogans.explanation: The idea behind this slogan is to approach our spiritual practice with a sense of commitment and dedication. This means not just going through the motions, or treating our practice as a casual hobby or pastime. Instead, we should strive to bring our full attention and effort to our practice, and to be fully engaged and present in each moment. By training wholeheartedly, we can avoid getting distracted or disillusioned, and we can make the most of the opportunities that our practice provides for personal growth and transformation.

slogans.title: Liberate yourself by examining and analyzing: Know your own mind with honesty and fearlessness
slogans.explanation: This slogan reminds us to look deeply and honestly at our own minds and emotions. This means not avoiding or denying our negative thoughts and feelings, but instead examining them closely and without judgment. By doing this, we can learn to understand the causes and conditions that give rise to our negative emotions, and we can develop the skills and insights to transform them. By liberating ourselves in this way, we can overcome our own limitations and develop a more profound sense of inner freedom and well-being.

slogans.title: Don't wallow in self-pity
slogans.explanation: This slogan urges us to avoid getting caught up in self-absorption. This means not indulging in negative thoughts or emotions, and not allowing ourselves to be consumed by feelings of victimhood or helplessness. Instead, we should strive to cultivate a sense of perspective and gratitude, and to focus on the positive aspects of our lives and the ways that we can help others. By not wallowing in self-pity, we can avoid getting stuck in unproductive or harmful patterns of thinking, and we can cultivate a more positive and compassionate outlook.

slogans.title: Don't be jealous
slogans.explanation: The meaning of this slogan is that, in order to cultivate mindfulness and compassion, we need to avoid jealousy and other harmful emotions. Jealousy is the feeling of resentment or envy towards someone who has something that we want, and it can lead us to compare ourselves negatively with others, or to wish them harm. By avoiding jealousy, we can cultivate a sense of contentment and gratitude, and we can focus on our own spiritual growth and well-being, rather than getting caught up in comparisons and competition. By doing this, we can develop a more positive and compassionate outlook, and we can cultivate a deeper sense of inner peace and fulfillment.

slogans.title: Don't be frivolous
slogans.explanation: The idea behind this slogan is that, in order to cultivate mindfulness and compassion, we need to avoid being frivolous or superficial in our approach to spiritual practice. This means not taking our practice lightly, or treating it as just another form of entertainment or distraction. Instead, we should approach our practice with seriousness and sincerity, and be willing to put in the time and effort required to make progress on the path. By not being frivolous, we can avoid getting sidetracked or discouraged, and we can develop a more profound and lasting connection to the spiritual teachings and practices.

slogans.title: Don't expect applause
slogans.explanation: This slogan reminds us that in order to cultivate mindfulness and compassion, we need to be willing to let go of our attachment to recognition and praise from others. This means not seeking applause or validation from others, and not letting our self-worth depend on the opinions or approval of others. Instead, we should strive to cultivate a sense of self-acceptance and inner contentment, and to approach our practice with humility and gratitude. By not expecting applause, we can avoid getting caught up in the ego-driven desire for recognition, and we can focus on the true purpose and benefits of our practice.
